ui.qs: Tap the mic and say the word
ui.nm: No microphone here. Practice with pairs or dictation instead.

vow.x: Spanish has only five vowels, a, e, i, o, u, and each one always sounds the same: short, clear and steady, with no glide to a second sound (unlike English “go”). Say “casa” and “solo” keeping your mouth still from start to end.

rr.x: A single r between vowels is a quick tap of the tongue, like the “tt” in American “butter”: “pero”. At the start of a word, or when written rr, it is a roll: “rojo”, “perro”. One letter changes the meaning: “pero” (but) and “perro” (dog).

bv.t: b and v sound the same
bv.x: The letters b and v stand for one sound. At the start of a word or after m or n it is a firm /b/ (“vaca”, “bola”). Between vowels the lips barely touch (“uva”, “lobo”). Never put your teeth on your lip like the English v. Which letter to write is spelling, not sound.

seseo.t: c, z and s: one sound
seseo.x: In Latin American Spanish, c (before e or i), z and s are all the same /s/: “cielo”, “zapato”, “casa”. There is no English “th” sound. So “casa” and “caza” sound identical; context gives the meaning and spelling has to be learned.

stress.x: Stress falls on the second-to-last syllable if the word ends in a vowel, n or s; otherwise on the last one. An accent mark breaks the rule and shows the stressed vowel: “papa” (potato) and “papá” (dad), “canto” (I sing) and “cantó” (he sang). Stress can change the meaning.

link.x: Spanish flows: a vowel at the end of a word joins the vowel that starts the next one with no pause. “la hora” sounds like “lahora” and “mi amigo” like “miamigo”. Do not stop between words.

jg.x: j, and g before e or i, is a breathy /x/ made at the back of the throat, like a strong “h”: “jarra”, “gente”. g before a, o, u is a hard /g/: “gato”. To keep g hard before e or i, write gu and do not say the u: “guerra”.

hq.x: ñ is like “ny” in “canyon”: “año”. ll and y sound like the English “y” or a soft “j”: “pollo”. h is always silent: “hola”, “hora”. qu is /k/ and the u is silent: “queso”. ch is as in “chico”.
